The provided text discusses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its subfield, machine learning, highlighting applications such as voice recognition (Siri) and autonomous vehicles. To enrich this context with database-related knowledge, we can link these concepts to how data is stored, retrieved, and processed in modern database systems.

For instance, machine learning algorithms rely heavily on large datasets for training, which are typically stored in relational databases (SQL) or NoSQL databases (like MongoDB or Cassandra) depending on the data structure. Voice recognition systems like Siri utilize natural language processing (NLP) models that query vast linguistic databases to interpret user intent. Similarly, autonomous vehicles depend on real-time data ingestion from sensors, which is often managed by time-series databases or in-memory databases to ensure low-latency decision-making. These database technologies provide the foundational infrastructure that allows AI systems to learn from experience and interact effectively with humans and their environments.
